paper_type_evidence.quote: Our work focuses on pattern speeds from the stellar mass surface density ($\Sigma_{\ast}$) from MUSE, but we also study the application of this method to ISM tracers
Whilst we base the majority of this study on pattern speeds derived from stellar kinematics, the PHANGS-ALMA data set in particular offers a much larger sample size.

question.value: Can the Tremaine-Weinberg method give reliable (bar) pattern speeds from PHANGS-MUSE stellar mass and velocity maps for 19 nearby galaxies, do ISM tracers (Halpha, ALMA CO) give the same pattern speeds, and how do pattern speeds and co-rotation radii relate to global galaxy parameters?

evidence.quote: We apply the Tremaine-Weinberg method to 19 nearby galaxies using stellar mass surface densities and velocities derived from the PHANGS-MUSE survey, to calculate (primarily bar) pattern speeds
Thus, we conclude that it is inadvisable to use “pattern speeds” derived from ISM kinematics.
We make use of $^{12}$CO($J=2{-}1$) maps (hereafter “CO” for brevity) from the PHANGS-ALMA survey.
We use cubes combined with all available data from the 12m and 7m arrays, and total power (TP) observations.
In total, 69 of our galaxies have 12m+7m+TP data, 7 have 12m+7m, 7 have 7m+TP, and 1 has 7m only.

analysis_steps.goal: Assemble surface brightness and velocity maps

method.value: Use MUSE stellar mass and velocity maps, MUSE Halpha maps, and PHANGS-ALMA CO moment 0 and moment 1 maps (broad masks, highest resolution) with error maps

evidence.quote: The cubes are then collapsed into standard moment 0 (integrated intensity) and moment 1 (intensity-weighted velocity), along with error maps.
(MUSE stellar mass and velocity, MUSE H$\alpha$, and ALMA CO, collectively referred to as “kinematic maps”)

key_parameters.value: Broad masks for ALMA moment maps

evidence.quote: We opt to use broad, rather than strict maps, to maximise our completeness (at the cost of increased noise).

key_parameters.value: MUSE stellar kinematics and stellar populations fit on Voronoi bins to continuum S/N of 35

evidence.quote: Both of these stages are performed on Voronoi binned data to a stellar continuum signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) of 35, to maximise reliability.

assumptions.value: Single stellar population fit; averaging over populations does not bias results since stellar mass is dominated by old stars

evidence.quote: The DAP fits only a single stellar population, so the stellar masses and velocities are an average of young and older stars.

validation.value: Negligible impact on results from strict vs broad masking in most cases

evidence.quote: We find a negligible impact on our results using these different masking schemes in most cases.

method.value: Mask MUSE foreground stars, subtract systemic velocity from ALMA moment 1, remove slits not crossing the bar, symmetrise each integral

evidence.quote: We therefore remove any pixels with $|v| > 300\,{\rm km\,s}^{-1}$.
We estimate the systemic velocity using PAFit (cite: 2006Krajnovic), and subtract it from the ALMA velocity field (moment 1) map.
This is done by removing any slits that do not at least partially cover the bar.

key_parameters.value: |v| > 300 km/s relative to systemic removed (MUSE only)

evidence.quote: We therefore remove any pixels with $|v| > 300\,{\rm km\,s}^{-1}$.

key_parameters.value: Each integral symmetrised to run from -x0 to x0

evidence.quote: we make sure each integral goes from $-x_0$ to $x_0$.
This cut is arbitrary, and may need to be tailored for other data sets.

validation.value: Recovered pattern speeds with masked or non-masked stars not significantly different

evidence.quote: However, we find that the recovered pattern speeds with masked or non-masked stars are not significantly different;

analysis_steps.goal: Compute Tremaine-Weinberg integrals and fit slope

method.value: Place boxcar pseudo-slits parallel to the line of nodes, compute intensity-weighted velocity and position per slit, fit slope of <v> vs <x> = Omega_P sin(i)

evidence.quote: In this work, we take $h(y)$ to be a boxcar function from $y-{\rm d}y$ to $y+{\rm d}y$, to represent a pseudo-slit parallel to the line of nodes.
Thus, taking a number of slits and plotting $\langle v \rangle$ versus $\langle x \rangle$ yields a straight line with a slope equivalent to $\Omega_{\rm P} \sin(i)$.

key_parameters.value: Slits as long as possible and 1 arcsec wide

evidence.loc: 3.3 Effects of slit length and width on recovered pattern speeds
evidence.quote: Motivated by these results, we opt to make each individual slit as long as possible, and 1$''$ wide to approximately match the resolution of the data.

key_parameters.value: Tested slit lengths 10 to 150 arcsec and widths 0.5 to 10 arcsec

evidence.loc: 3.3 Effects of slit length and width on recovered pattern speeds
evidence.quote: We use a number of slit lengths, from 10$''$ to 150$''$
The galaxy disk is flat;
The disk contains a single, well-defined pattern speed;
The tracer obeys the continuity equation.

fitting.value: Orthogonal Distance Regression (scipy.odr) with per-pixel errors summed in quadrature in both <x> and <v>

evidence.quote: These are then propagated into the fitting routine using Orthogonal Distance Regression (ODR), which allows us to effectively account for errors in both $\langle x \rangle$ and $\langle v \rangle$.

validation.value: Slit length/width convergence tests for each galaxy; measured pattern speeds converge as slits become longer, slit width has minimal impact

evidence.loc: 3.3 Effects of slit length and width on recovered pattern speeds
evidence.quote: We find that the measured pattern speeds tend to converge as the slits become longer (typically, slightly longer than the bar).

evidence.loc: 3.3 Effects of slit length and width on recovered pattern speeds
evidence.quote: We also find that the slit width has a minimal impact on the recovered pattern speed

method.value: Perturb line of nodes and galaxy centre by their measured errors, 1000 bootstraps, quote median and 16th/84th percentiles

evidence.quote: We do this via a Monte-Carlo method, perturbing the line of nodes and the galaxy centre by the measured errors (cite: 2020Lang).
We use 1000 bootstraps, measure the pattern speed for each of these iterations, and quote the pattern speed as the median of this distribution

key_parameters.value: 1000 bootstraps; inclination and distance errors not included

evidence.quote: We do not include uncertainties from the inclination or distance in our uncertainty for the pattern speeds.

assumptions.value: Position-angle error dominates the error budget

evidence.quote: and that it is the error in the position angle that dominates

method.value: A posteriori flags Q=1 to 4 assigned independently by three authors per tracer; final flag is the mode, or highest flag if all disagree; Q=1 or 2 are 'well-constrained'

evidence.quote: This flagging is performed independently on each tracer by three of the authors, and our final flag is the mode of these three flags.
we will define “well-constrained” Tremaine-Weinberg values as having $Q=1$ or 2

key_parameters.value: Q=1 single well-defined slope converged and stable with decreasing slit width; Q=2 clear multiple slopes; Q=3 poor fit; Q=4 insufficient data

evidence.quote: Single, well defined slope: integrals have converged, pattern speed is stable with decreasing slit width;

analysis_steps.goal: Test ISM tracers with a null (no-pattern) axisymmetric model

method.value: Axisymmetrise CO velocity (from Lang et al. rotation-curve fits) and surface brightness (annulus averages), blank pixels where emission is not detected, apply TW method to get Omega_null; compare with Omega_clump from real CO data; repeat with Halpha and with ~5 arcsec CO; toy density-wave models

evidence.quote: For the velocity field, we project the fits from (cite: 2020Lang) into the frame of the galaxy, and for the CO data we take the average surface brightness within a number of annuli.
We then mimic the incomplete coverage of these maps by blanking pixels in these axisymmetrised profiles where emission is not detected

key_parameters.value: Higher resolution (~1 arcsec) vs lower resolution (~5 arcsec) ALMA data compared

evidence.quote: we compare $\Omega_{\rm clump}$ from the higher resolution ($\sim$1$''$) and lower resolution ($\sim$5$''$) ALMA data.

assumptions.value: No pattern speed is present in the axisymmetrised maps, so any deviation is due to incomplete coverage and clumpy morphology

evidence.quote: In this case, there is no pattern speed present in these maps, and any deviation is simply due to the incomplete CO coverage and the non-axisymmetry of the CO morphology.

validation.value: Points lie near the 1:1 relation of Omega_null vs Omega_clump; low and high resolution give much the same result

evidence.quote: As we can see, the points tend to lie close to the ${1\!:\!1}$ relation
This indicates that this effect is endemic to the use of CO, and not simply due to the high resolution of our data.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare ISM-tracer and stellar pattern speeds

method.value: Define pattern speed difference = (Omega_clump - Omega_P)/Omega_P for galaxies well-constrained in both stellar mass and the ISM tracer (9 galaxies for each of Halpha and CO)

evidence.quote: We compare values flagged as well-constrained in both the stellar mass, and the ISM tracer in question (for both H$\alpha$ and CO, this leaves us with 9 galaxies).

validation.value: Omega_clump systematically higher than Omega_P by more than the ~10% errors

evidence.quote: Typically, we find that $\Omega_{\rm clump}$ is higher than $\Omega_{\rm P}$

method.value: Convert CO rotation curves (Lang et al.) to angular velocity and find where it equals Omega_P for co-rotation; ILR/OLR from Omega_P = Omega(R) -/+ kappa/2 with smooth splines; deproject bar length and form R_CR/R_bar and h_r/R_CR

evidence.quote: By converting the rotation velocity to an angular velocity, $\Omega (R)$, the co-rotation radius is simply where the angular velocity is equal to the pattern speed.
In this case, to avoid issues with numerical derivatives, we use smooth splines fitted to the rotation curves.

key_parameters.value: Consecutive crossing points within 2 sigma are associated with the same R_CR; mean taken as nominal value, range as uncertainty

evidence.quote: For these points, we associate these to the same $R_{\rm CR}$ if they are within $2\sigma$, and we take the mean of them as the nominal values, with the range as the uncertainty.

assumptions.value: Observed CO velocity profile is a proxy for the circular velocity

evidence.quote: We use this observed velocity profile as a proxy for the true circular velocity of the galaxy

validation.value: Rotation curves from CO, Halpha and stars typically similar; R_CR errors similar to gravitational torque analysis

evidence.quote: Typically, the rotation curves derived from the CO maps are very similar to those derived from H$\alpha$ and stars in our sample
These errors are similar to those obtained using gravitational torque analysis (cite: 2016Querejeta).

analysis_steps.goal: Correlate pattern speeds and bar properties with global parameters

method.value: Kendall tau correlations between Omega_P, R_CR, R_bar, R, S_bar and projection or global galaxy parameters, with Monte Carlo perturbation of values by errors

evidence.quote: For $10{,}000$ realisations, we perturb each value by its associated errors in both $x$ and $y$, and repeat the $\tau$ calculation.

key_parameters.value: Only points with relative Omega_P error <= 0.5 (removes NGC 7496)

evidence.quote: but in this work we find that this removes only one galaxy (NGC 7496).

validation.value: Correlation significant only if larger than its 1 sigma Monte Carlo spread; checked for dependence on inclination and Delta PA

evidence.quote: If the correlation is larger than this 1$\sigma$ error, then the correlation is significant.

evidence.quote: this method erroneously gives a signal that is simply the angular frequency at a representative radius set by the distribution of these clumps

claims.hypothesis: Can TW applied to PHANGS-MUSE stellar mass and velocity maps yield reliable pattern speeds for nearby galaxies?
claims.experiment: Applied TW with 1 arcsec boxcar slits and ODR fits to 19 MUSE galaxies, quality-flagged by three authors
claims.result: 10 of 19 galaxies well-constrained (Q=1 or 2); median Omega_P of 30 (+10/-9) km/s/kpc
claims.finding: About half of the stellar-mass-based pattern speeds are reliable, and they agree with previous literature values

evidence.quote: After quality checks, we find that around half (10) of these stellar mass-based measurements are reliable.
For those galaxies, we find good agreement between our results and previously published pattern speeds

claims.hypothesis: Do clumpy ISM tracers (Halpha, CO) give valid pattern speeds with TW?
claims.experiment: Compared Omega_null from axisymmetrised blanked maps to Omega_clump from real CO and Halpha, and Omega_clump to stellar Omega_P for 9 galaxies
claims.result: Omega_clump lies near Omega_null and is higher than Omega_P by ~20% (Halpha) and ~40-50% (CO)
claims.finding: ISM-derived 'pattern speeds' are an angular frequency set by clump distribution and should not be used as Omega_P proxies

evidence.quote: it is clear from this exercise that $\Omega_{\rm clump}$ and $\Omega_{\rm P}$ are systematically different quantities, and thus $\Omega_{\rm clump}$ should not be used as a proxy for $\Omega_{\rm P}$.

claims.hypothesis: Are commonly assumed ratios R_CR/R_bar ~ 1.2 and h_r/R_CR ~ 3 consistent with measured co-rotation radii?
claims.experiment: Derived R_CR from Omega_P and CO rotation curves, deprojected bar lengths, compared ratios
claims.result: R about 1.1 to 1.3 and h_r/R_CR about 2.6 to 2.7 with large scatter
claims.finding: Sample is consistent with the common values given small-number statistics

evidence.quote: so our values of $\mathcal{R}$ are, on average, consistent with the expected value of 1.2.
Again, given the small number statistics we conclude our sample to be consistent with a value for $h_r/R_{\rm CR}$ of 3.

claims.hypothesis: Do pattern speeds and bar properties correlate with global galaxy parameters?
claims.experiment: Kendall tau with Monte Carlo error perturbation for up to 9 galaxies
claims.result: Higher Omega_P in later types and gas-rich galaxies, lower in bulge-dominated; no significant trend with bar strength or total stellar mass surface density; higher Omega_P goes with smaller R_CR
claims.finding: Confirms several earlier trends but not all; authors treat the analysis as exploratory given the small sample

evidence.quote: Given that our sample is still small, we see this investigation as exploratory
In particular, we find no correlation between bar strength and pattern speed, nor between total stellar mass surface density and pattern speed.

limitations_admitted.value: TW recovers only a single pattern speed; multiple pattern speeds (bars and spirals) not separated

limitations_admitted.value: Bias from secondary spiral pattern not quantified; needs simulations with known ground truth

limitations_admitted.value: Small number statistics limit correlation analysis

evidence.quote: Given that we are only confident in pattern speeds measured using stellar masses and velocities, this work is hindered by low number statistics.

limitations_admitted.value: Resonance radii approximate; observed CO velocity overestimates circular velocity where non-axisymmetry dominates; inclination and distance errors not in pattern speed uncertainty

evidence.quote: As such, we highlight that these resonance locations are approximations, but represent our best estimation of the true value.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 10 galaxies with reliable stellar pattern speeds, 9 for correlations; correlation conclusions are fragile
Quality flags depend on subjective by-eye judgement by three authors
Omega_clump vs Omega_P offset is inferred from a handful of toy models and 9 galaxies; the true bias mechanism is not demonstrated with simulations
Internal inconsistencies in the text: CO offset ~50% in abstract vs ~40% in body; R 1.1 vs 1.3 and h_r/R_CR 2.6 vs 2.7 in different sections
Rotation curves from CO used for resonances, which may overestimate circular velocity in bars
ALMA CO data are internal DR products and MUSE DR 2.0 is described only in a paper in preparation
